# 1 Enoch Chapter 64 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 64:1 — 'terrible' vs. 'terrifying' for the appearance of the Watchers

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "terrible-ones" | Literal; Ge'ez ferahawi = fear-inspiring, dreadful |
| LOGOS | "terrible ones" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "terrifying ones" | 'Terrifying' is more active — they actively cause terror |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'terrible' (EMET/LOGOS). 'Terrible' in its archaic sense (= causing terror, dread) is the precise English equivalent of Ge'ez ferahawi. 'Terrifying' (PNEUMA) has the same meaning but LOGOS's more formal register suits this context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 64:2 — 'the sons of men could not preserve themselves' — the nature of the human failure

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sons-of-men have-not-been-able-to-preserve-themselves from-them" | Literal; passive failure |
| LOGOS | "the sons of men have not been able to preserve themselves from them" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "The sons of men could not resist them" | 'Resist' sharpens the sense; active rather than passive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Preserve themselves' is the Ge'ez idiom — it implies self-discipline and separation, not merely military resistance. PNEUMA's 'resist' is accurate but misses the purity/holiness connotation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
